characters.name: Richard Castle
characters.description: Bestselling-but-bored playboy mystery writer who, after helping Kate Beckett and the NYPD find a killer basing his murders off his books, pulled strings to get himself attached to Beckett's unit,ostensibly to research a character based on herbutreallybecause he likes solving mysteries and is attracted to Beckett. He eventually becomes a Private Investigator in Season 7. Action Dad: He handles himself well against thugs and that doesn't take away how much loves his daughter and being protective of her. See his brief partnership with Slaughter for details. Action Survivor: The more time he spends with the police force, the better he gets at surviving trouble. Actor Allusion: With a dose ofCelebrity Paradox. While the show is never specifically named, Castle frequently indicates that he's a fan ofFirefly.

characters.name: Kate Beckett
characters.description: Brilliant police detective with an interest in and knack for solving left-field cases, and an overt exasperation for Castle's presence. She's a fan of Castle's novels and she doesnotwant him to know this.He does. The Ace: Youngest female detective in NYPD history, highest case closure rate, highly competent marksman and hand to hand combatant. Tremendously talented as an investigator and interrogator. Action Girl: Police detective that specializes in tracking murderers. Affectionate Pickpocket: In "The Limey", she lifts a golden case from a man's pocketwhile dancing with him. It had his prints on it. Agent Scully: Never ever accepts supernatural explanations. However, she does like havingCastlearound because his wacky explanations and unorthodox approach to cases push her to think outside the box.

characters.name: Martha Rodgers
characters.description: Actor Allusion: In the episode "One Life to Lose", which concerns a murder related to a soap opera, she is revealed to have had a brief but very eventful stint acting in another soap opera before her Broadway years. In the 80s, Susan Sullivan had a long-running role as Maggie Channing onFalcon Crest. December–December Romance: She's perfectly willing to sleep with aSilver Fox; her opening scene has her talking about her "gray-dar." Fiery Redhead: Is a redhead and is able to keep Castle in line through force of personality. Gold Digger: Martha isnotone of these, despite her penchant for wealthy older men; she was, however, the victim of one, which forced her to move into her son and granddaughter's apartment. She's also not shy about charging vast amounts to her son's credit card, much to his exasperation, but it's made abundantly clear that she loves him for far more than his purchasing power. She also tries in "Lucky Stiff" to turn down the significant amount of money left to her by a deceased boyfriend. Good Parents: Very much like her son in that she might be quite flighty and a little nuts in many aspects of her life but she deeply loves her son and, despite a few missteps, seems to have done a good job raising him.

characters.name: Alexis Castle
characters.description: Bratty Teenage Daughter: Averted. She's one of the most likable teenage characters on television, a fact of which Castle isverymuch aware and thanks his lucky stars for. Commuting on a Bus: Once she goes to college, she's in and out of episodes. The Cutie: She's got her fair share of charm and cuteness. Daddy's Girl: Not spoiled, but loved. Damsel in Distress: In the fifth season episode "Target", Alexis is a victim in a kidnapping plot.She and her fellow victim actively try to manage the situation and escape.

characters.name: Johanna Beckett
characters.description: Crusading Lawyer: Johanna worked for a lot of causes during her life, including attempting to clean up Washington Heights and working with the Justice Initiative to re-open closed cases and exonerate the wrongly convicted. Death by Origin Story: Kate Beckett decided to pursue law enforcement rather than pursuing her supreme court dreams due to her mother's murder. Kate even lampshades this when she tells Castle what happened, saying Nikki Heat has a backstory now. Posthumous Character: She died years before the first season, so anything about her is told through other characters.

characters.name: Jim Beckett
characters.description: The Alcoholic: 5 years sober as of the beginning of the series. From Bad to Worse: First his wife is murdered which goes unsolved. Then his daughter and only child joins the police driven by an obsession with the case while working a inherently dangerous job. He outright tells Kate that he didn't sleep soundly for a year after his graduated the academy and thought of her "in the dark" every time he heard sirens. Good Parents: He and Kate have a good relationship, with him understanding and supporitive of her career choice and her drive to solve her mother's murder.

characters.name: Jackson Hunt
characters.description: Disappeared Dad: Martha knew nothing of him and never saw Jackson after that night, not even knowing his name. Unlike most cases, Castle isn't bothered by this due to being a grown man and his not knowing anything allows Rick to imagine his father to be anything or anyone.Under normal circumstances he'd be thrilled to learn his old man is a legit spy master. No Name Given: "Jackson Hunt" is a cover name, something he freely admits as soon as he meets Castle. He never gives his real nameeven after he reveals himself as Castle's father. Old Master: A long-time spy with much experience who's pulled theBig Damn Heroesact at least twice to rescuehis son Richard. Papa Wolf: Exploiting this trait towardhis son Richard and granddaughter Alexisis how his archenemy Gregor Volkov got him to come out of hiding. Walking Spoiler: Given his profession and his relatioship to the story, it's pretty much impossible to give any information on the man.

characters.name: Javier Esposito
characters.description: Agent Scully: Within the Ryan/Esposito partnership, Espo is the one to refute Ryan's crazy, Castle-inspired theories. Bash Brothers: With Ryan. Because You Were Nice to Me: He was a juvenile delinquent until a teacher took an interest in him, sent him to the marines, helped him become a cop. As a result he pays it forward to a kid being used as a thief by an older criminal in season five. Beta Couple: He and Lanie date for a while in season three and four while Castle and Beckett are still dancing around each other, but panic and break up when they double-date with Ryan and his then-fiancee Jenny and she asks them whenthey'regetting hitched. (Though Lanie admitsthey still occasionallygettogether for a booty calleven after they've broken up.) Beware the Silly Ones: Usually, he's pretty offbeat, laid back, and generally irreverent, but when his friends, kids, or innocents are threatened, he turns into a pretty terrifying badass. A couple of victimized women in his cases also triggered his protective tendencies, and he went out of his way to solve their problems.

characters.name: Kevin Ryan
characters.description: Esposito's partner who also takes great pleasure in winding Beckett up. In later seasons, he's more likely to side with Castle's wacky theories than any self-respecting officer of the law should. Action Dad:By the end of the series, he's a father of two. Badass Boast: In "Knockdown".Ryan:(while being tortured in ice water)Listen, assclown. I went to Catholic school for twelve years. Hell, they used to do this to me for talking in class. Bash Brothers: With Esposito. Berserk Button: As shown in "Kick the Ballistics", do nottake Kevin Ryan's service weapon, and especially do not use said weapon to kill an innocent young woman. He will find you andend you.

characters.name: Lanie Parish
characters.description: The medical examiner and Beckett's best friend, who has an inkling that there's more to Castle and Beckett's relationship than meets the eye. Advertised Extra: Despite being billed as a main character, Lanie's primary role on the show was to beThe Coronerwho gives the team information about theBody of the Week, with storylines of her own being very rare. She's also more than likely to either miss several episodes at a time, or only make brief appearances in the episodes she's featured in. The Coroner: She opens the dead guys looking for clues. D-Cup Distress: Yes and no. She mentioned in one episode how she always wanted to be a ballerina as a child, but had to stop when she turned 13 and "the girls" made her too top-heavy to continue. Since then, she decided they have their perks. Deadpan Snarker: Lanie is prone to delivering sassy and sarcastic remarks every now and then.

characters.name: Roy Montgomery
characters.description: The captain of the 12th Precinct devoted to protecting his people regardless of political fallout. Roy allows Castle to shadow Beckett on cases partly because of pressure from the mayor but primarily because he sees Castle as a good man and healthy for Beckett. The Atoner:As revealed in the season 3 finale "Knockout", he was a part of the conspiracy that led to Beckett's mother's death. He met her in the records room going over the case's evidence, and took her under his wing, guiding her to be the head detective of the 12th Precinct. He finally earns his redemption by taking out Hal Lockwood, the man who works for the man who ordered Beckett's mother's death, at the cost of his own life. Benevolent Boss: While he does have his scary moments, overall Roy is pretty laid back about rules and deeply cares for the personal well-being of his cops. He also has no problem responding to the goofy questions Castle asks. This is especially noticeable when you compare him tohis replacement, Captain Gates. Big Good: He's Beckett's boss which makes him the head good guy. Deadpan Snarker: "Sir, can I talk to you for a second?" "Nope."

characters.name: Victoria "Iron" Gates
characters.description: Bait-and-Switch Tyrant: Played with; she's no Roy Montgomery, but she seems to be softening towards Castle somewhat and is a dedicated officer who isverygood at her job. Big Good: After replacing Montgomery, she becomes the head good guy. Black Boss Lady: The stern type. By-the-Book Cop: Has no intention of letting her cops get away with playing fast and loose with the rules. Contrasting Sequel Main Character: To Montgomery, in regards to their relationship with Castle. Montgomery kept Castle around because hewantedto and thought he would be a good influence on Beckett. Gates is forced to keep Castle around by the mayor, and thinks (at first anyway) that Kate would be a better detective without him.

characters.name: Hayley Shipton
characters.description: A quick-witted, free-spirited, former Scotland Yard police officer who works as a security specialist and is not afraid to cross lines to get things done. Action Girl: She manages to hold her own in combat with a professional hitwoman. Though she isn't quite as skilled as Beckett, who kills said hitwoman. Deadpan Snarker: Pretty much the majority of Hayley's dialogue consists of her making a witty or sarcastic remark of some kind. The Mentor: She seems to play this role to Alexis a bit, teaching her some of the tricks of the trade in terms of being a PI operating without help from the police. She also attempts to teach Castle that lesson, though it doesn't entirely stick. Only in It for the Money: She initially claims this, as she only gets paid if she delivers for her clients. Though she does seem to enjoy working with Castle and develops a genuine bond with Alexis. Though Castle does still pay her for her services.

characters.name: M.E. Sidney Perlmutter
characters.description: A second coroner introduced in season two. Grumpy and snarky. Where as Lanie will snark at Castle in a friendly manner, Perlmutter will simply snark at Castle in general. The Coroner: Like Lanie, he also opens up dead people to look for clues. Deadpan Snarker: Has shown being able to snark back at most everyone. Foil: To more regular coroner Lanie. Both are skilled professionals. Lanie is naturally personable and gets on well with the detectives and Castle, while Perlmutter is grumpy and generally irritated by other characters (particularly Castle). Jerkass: While the other characters snark at Castle in a good-humored fashion, Perlmutter is more mean-spirited.

characters.name: Tory Ellis
characters.description: An NYPD computer tech whose appearances are limited to explaining whatever tech is involved in the case of the week. She is good friends with Lanie. Ascended Extra: Originally she was just an unnamed video tech who popped up once in a while but is now a named character who appears in most episodes and has become a respected member ofThe Team. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: She's gone as of Season 8, with nary a mention of what happened to her. A Day in the Limelight: The episode 'Kill Switch' is the first one to give emphasis on her friendship with Lanie as well as being the first episode she appears for the entirety of. Fake Guest Star: She is the only member of the main group NOT in the opening credits.

characters.name: Meredith
characters.description: Crazy in the Head, Crazy in the Bed: Castle hasSex with the Exwith her for this reason. While Meredith is shown to be impulsive and irresponsible, Castle finds sex with her great. Beckett is less than impressed when Castle explains this to her. Fair-Weather Family: Meredith is a flighty actress who had an affair, moved to Malibu, and divorced Castle before the first episode. Her immaturity meant that Castle,of all people, was granted sole custody of Alexis. Alexis, for her part, is less phased by her mother's absence than by her mother's presence since, in spite of loving her, she's anAmazingly Embarrassing Parentand her father gave her everything she ever needed.In "Always Buy Retail" Meredith visits and intends to move back to New York, partly to be closer to Alexis but also because she wasn't finding desirable roles in LA. While visiting, she pulls Alexis out of school without her daughter's consent for a shopping spree and calls Castle in the middle of a huge case, prompting Castle to ensure a role in an indie film for her which makes her change her mind on moving back.In "Significant Others", she shows up unannounced saying she's there to take care of Alexis while she has mono, but with the ulterior motive of scoping out Castle's latest muse and girlfriend, Kate Beckett. In "Always Buy Retail" Meredith visits and intends to move back to New York, partly to be closer to Alexis but also because she wasn't finding desirable roles in LA. While visiting, she pulls Alexis out of school without her daughter's consent for a shopping spree and calls Castle in the middle of a huge case, prompting Castle to ensure a role in an indie film for her which makes her change her mind on moving back. In "Significant Others", she shows up unannounced saying she's there to take care of Alexis while she has mono, but with the ulterior motive of scoping out Castle's latest muse and girlfriend, Kate Beckett. Fiery Redhead: A disposition that her daughter partly inherited.

characters.name: Gina Cowell
characters.description: Amicable Exes: Is still his agent despite being divorced and gets played straight again after their second failed relationship. Good Stepmother: She got along well with Alexis, if their interaction during Gina and Castle's second romance is any indication. A Lighter Shade of Grey: Compared to Meredith, Castle's other ex-wife. While both are demanding and,at least according to Castle,given toGold Diggerbehaviour Gina is far more sensible and less selfish. Also while Meredith cheating on Castle ended their marriage there's no indication of such on Gina's part. Sex with the Ex: She and Castle start up their relationship again at the end of Season 2 but break it off after several fights later in Season 3. Shipper on Deck: Like everyone else, she can tell that, at the least, Castle is into Beckett and encourages him to sleep with her...mainly because she sees his "consulting" as distracting him from doing his job and wants him to get to work.

characters.name: Kyra Blaine
characters.description: Amicable Exes: She and Castle hold no animosity at all toward each other, seeming to be just rather wistful regarding their former relationship. Nice Girl: Kyra is never anything but pleasant throughout her episode, withour first impression of herbeing her admonishing her uptight mother that she's more concerned for the wellbeing of a missing bridesmaid than the effect it's having on her wedding.

characters.name: Josh Davidson
characters.description: Romantic False Lead: He's there to get in the way of the Castle/Beckett relationship. Satellite Character: He only appears rarely to meet up with Beckett.

characters.name: Jenny O'Malley
characters.description: Happily Married: Ryan and Jenny have the occasional falling out but nothing they can't get past and they're generally nothing but happy. Sickeningly Sweethearts: She and Ryan adore each other and don't mind letting everyone know that.

characters.name: Madison Queller
characters.description: Emotional Regression: Despite being a quite mature and accomplished woman when she thinks Beckett has taken her in for questioning just to stop her going out with Castle the two end up squabbling like the teenagers they were when they met.

characters.name: Damian Westlake
characters.description: Broken Pedestal: His encouragement early in life set Castle on his life path and left Castle with a deep admiration for Damian. Suffice to say he doesn't deserve it. Ignored Epiphany: Late in his episode, he admits that he has been a generally awful person.Though this doesn't make him confess to arranging his father's murder.

characters.name: Pi
characters.description: New-Age Retro Hippie:Downplayed,as he's not wearing tie-dyed shirts, affecting the "stoner" accent, failing to wash or otherwise living the most obvious stereotypes but he does have the vibe.

characters.name: Det. Tom Demming
characters.description: Romantic False Lead: Demming mostly exists to make Castle jealous. Not as generic as some examples though, as he does have more to do in a couple of episodes, being a suspect in his first appearance and aiding in another investigation where the murder also featured a robbery.

characters.name: Dr. Burke
characters.description: There Are No Therapists:An aversion.Beckett had mandatory counselling after being shot and decides to keep going to see him and Dr. Burke is very helpful to her in working through a number of difficulties.

characters.name: Ike Thorton
characters.description: Determinator: Even beingframed as a dirty copdoesn't stop him on his mission.

characters.name: Mike Royce
characters.description: The Atoner: After his first apperance he's dedicated his life to helping out those in troublein large part to make up for giving into his greed and betraying Beckett. Implied Love Interest: Beckett says she was in love with him. It's never made explicit what exactly went on between the two but there's enough to suggest an actual relationship. Shipper on Deck: One of many who ship Beckett with Castle.

characters.name: Detective Slaughter
characters.description: Boisterous Bruiser: He's a loud, rude, and hard-drinking brawler. Casanova Wannabe: Hits on Beckett, an unnamed female ME, and perves off-screen on Alexis. He has zero on-screen success with any woman. Cowboy Cop: He's violent, reckless and basically the exact opposite of Beckett. Dirty Cop: Threatens a gangster by proxy into turning on his boss and leads him during the interrogation into saying what he needs to hear. Drives Like Crazy: Off-screen, but he apparently drives on the sidewalk.

characters.name: LT
characters.description: The Danza: He's only ever referred to asLTwith his credits given as Lt Tolliver his actor's name.

characters.name: Will Sorenson
characters.description: Romantic False Lead: The first of several potential romantic partners for Beckett to get in the way of her and Castle.

characters.name: Mark Fallon
characters.description: Real Tragedy, Fictional Victim: His wife died on United Airlines Flight 175, and he was on the phone with his wife when her plane crashed into the second tower on 9/11. As a result, he's an absolute hardass anti-terrorist DHS agent

characters.name: Sophia Turner
characters.description: Arc Villain:Revealed to be the true villain of the Pandora / Linchpin two parter. Turns out she's actually a Russian sleeper agent hired to infiltrate the CIA and createWorld War 3by killing the daughter of a Chinese finance minister, which would result in the destruction of America. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: Turner presents herself as a helpful CIA agent, who just so happens to be one of Castle's former muses.In reality, she's a Russian mercenary working to startWorld War 3.

characters.name: Serena Kaye
characters.description: Classy Cat-Burglar: Her background was this, specializing in "taking back" stolen or wrongfully seized artwork and returning it to their rightful owners. She still uses her equipment but now as her job as a retrieval specialist for an insurance company. Expy: OfCatherine Bannin/Vicki Andersonbeing an insurance investigator who works with the local cops with her sole job to retrieve stolen artwork back. Though she has some elements of Thomas Crown thrown in with a background as a thief. Reformed Criminal:A look into her past reveals that she's a former highly-skill thief who committed several thefts but never caught. She then made a career change to an insurance investigator,using her reputation as a bargaining chip to make use of retrieving stolen artwork.It should be noted that when asked about, not only does Serena admits to it butreveals everything she had stolen was already stolen artworkandwas simply returned to its rightful owners.

characters.name: Dick Coonan
characters.description: Actually, I Am Him: When he realises Beckett is prioritizing her mother's killer, he claims that he hired a hit man called "Rathborne" to commit the murder for him. This allows him to cut a deal for immunity in exchange for setting up another contract to lure Rathborne out. He has them wire $100,000 to his own offshore account but Rathborne never shows up to the location. However, as Dick is walking out with his immunity he mentionsBeckett's mother being the victim "Rathborne" supposedly killed. That's when Castle and Beckett realize that Coonan never hired a hit man; he was his own hit man. Cain and Abel:Downplayed,in that both brothers were violent criminals. His brother, Jack, found out he was smuggling drugs in the territory ofThe Irish Moband was ordered to kill him. Jack couldn't bring himself to murder his own brother... but Dick could. Calling Card: His favored method of murder is killing his victims with a precise thrust to the kidneys. However, he tries to mask this by stabbing the victim is several other places across the abdomen and torso to camouflage the skill of the initial killing strike. Particularly observant coroners still notice it and are able to use it to attribute kills to him though. He also always uses a USMC standard issue KA-BAR to stab them, honed so sharp it leaves traces of the blade in the wounds. Hostage Situation: In a desperate final bid to escape the 12th Precinct, he takes Castle hostage at gunpoint and tries to make it to the exit. Professional Killer: He was a special operations soldier in the First Gulf War and became a contract killer sometime afterwards. He eventually graduated into a drug kingpin but when he needed somebody dead he still did the job himself rather than pay for a hit man.

characters.name: Hal Lockwood
characters.description: Affably Evil: Quite polite and professional in the execution of his work, even assassinations and torture. Cold Sniper: His introduction is shooting adirty cop trying to go cleanmid confession, from a building across the street. Consummate Professional: Maintains a military discipline and methodology to his work. He speaks in code, covers his tracks and never shows an ounce of emotion. Hero Killer:Kills Captain Montgomery. Icy Blue Eyes: He's always giving the same emotionless stare.

characters.name: Vulcan Simmons
characters.description: The Dragon: While initially seeming to be aRed Herringin his first appearance, he ultimately is working as a senior lieutenant forWilliam Bracken.Not to be confused with the nickname for the mastermind detailed below. Scary Black Man: He cuts a very intimidating figure. You Have Outlived Your Usefulness: He eventually becomes a liability to "The Dragon."He is murdered to both remove him as a loose end and frame Beckett.

characters.name: The Dragon
characters.description: Affably Evil: Has polite small talk with Beckett and the crew, even though they've both planned on killing each other. Arch-Enemy: To Beckett, sincehe's the one whohad her mother killed. Big Bad: Serves as this forthe entire 'Beckett's Mother Conspiracy Arc', having been the politician who ordered her murder. Blackmail: This trope is pretty much how he ended up becoming successful in politics.After hearing about Raglan,Mc Callister, and Montgomery's kidnapping scheme, he threatened to have them arrested and charged unless they gave him a cut of the ransom money, so he could use it to fund his first political campaign. Consummate Liar: How he's managed to evade justice for decades.

characters.name: The Copycat
characters.description: Crazy-Prepared: Deconstructed as this is what definitively makes him as a suspect: he had an airtight alibi forallthe murders and even knew off the top of his head when they happened. Beckett points out that innocent people don't need alibis. Frame-Up: His plan was to frame one of his sister Allison's cases as a social worker as the killer to throw off the scent off him. Inheritance Murder: Harrison's business is failing, and with his sister out of the way, he inherits all of his father's money. Of course, given that his motive for these killings is revenge as stated below, the money is really more of a happy bonus. Serial Killings, Specific Target: Harrison killed two other people alongside his sister. Castle explains to Alexis that when the body count in these kinds of cases gets to three, police tend to stop looking for some connection to the victims and look for a crazy person like Kyle, who doesn't reallyneeda motive to kill people. Shown Their Work:SubvertedIn-Universeas this is the first thread which begins unraveling his scheme. While Harrison replicated the crimes from Castle's books enough the police realize the connection, he fails to geteverydetail right, which an obsessive fanaticSerial Killerwould never do.

characters.name: Nikki's Fan
characters.description: Arc Villain: Serves as this for the Tick, Tick, Tick / Boom 2 - parter. Arch-Nemesis: Views himself as one to "Nikki Heat" who is the fictional character from Castle's new book series. His obsession leads to him targeting Beckett, since she was the inspiration for the character, making her his perfect counterpart as a representation of a detective who was part-reality and part-fiction. Blaming the Victim: Blames his murders on "Nikki" for being unable to catch him and uses this to taunt Beckett and make her feel guilty. When she survives his bombing attempt he takes out his rage by killing a random woman and telling Beckett she wouldn't be dead if "Nikki" had just died like she was supposed to. Calling Card: He writes letters on the bullets he fires into his victims to send messages to taunt the NYPD. Frame-Up: Kills victims connected to the innocent Ben Conrad to make him look guilty and then makes Ben's death look like a suicide to fake his death.Did this previously in Seattle. To write his latest manuscript he killed several prostitutes for inspiration then hung a prime suspect and made it look like a suicide to escape.

characters.name: Radford Hayes
characters.description: Arc Villain:Eventually revealed to be this for the Setup/Countdown 2 - parter. Shell-Shocked Veteran: Hayes and his group are veterans who have gone off the deep end because they believed the United States stopped caring about the War on Terror, and plan to bomb NYC in the belief that it will stir up anti - terrorist sentiment across the US, and spark a renewed desire to continue the War on Terror in the Middle East.

characters.name: 3XK
characters.description: Arc Villain: Tyson first appears in season 3, lasting all the way up to season 7, showing up every other season to torment Castle. Arch-Enemy: To Castle because of the obession with proving himself smarter, for escaping, and also the Beckett kidnapping. Character Death:In "Reckoning", Tyson is killed with a sniper rifle by Esposito. He's not walking that one off. The Chessmaster: Proves to be highly intelligent and a master schemer, capable of developing elaborate plans toescape prison, frame Castle for murder, and erase his identity from the NYPD's system.There is a good reason why he's the only villain in the show's run to escape justice at the end of an episode. Hoist by His Own Petard:In a roundabout way, his addiction to complex murders that put him in the line of fire and his love of manipulating others ends up killing him. While Tyson finds it easy to get into people's heads to make them do what he wants, it never occurs to him that Castle could get inside his head and turn his own plan to lure Castle out against him. After seasons of playing other people, he gets played himself when Castle uses his need to have the last word in a complicated crime against him.

characters.name: Gregor Volkov
characters.description: Arc Villain: Serves as this for the Target / Hunt 2 - parter, having been the one who orchestrated Alexis' kidnapping. Crusading Widower: The reason that Volkov wants to kill Hunt is because he wants revenge after Hunt killed his wife. Former Regime Personnel: He was in theKGBbefore going into business for himself, presumably after the USSR disbanded. Revenge by Proxy: Volkov plots to get revenge on Jackson Hunt for the death of his wife by orchestrating the kidnapping of Alexis, who is Hunt'sgranddaughter.

characters.name: Brad Parker
characters.description: Arc Villain: Serves as this for the Valkyrie/Dreamworld 2 - parter. Crusading Widower: Parker wants revenge for the death of his wife. The Plague: Parker's plan involves a deadly military toxin by the name of Valkyrie.

characters.name: Kelly Niemen
characters.description: Abhorrent Admirer: She is completely obsessed with Beckett's face. Mad Doctor: Gave two people plastic surgery to impersonate Lanie and Esposito as part of a plan to steal Tyson's existing criminal records, and intended toremove Beckett's face as part of her own escape. Surgical Impersonation: Used her skills to create a "fake" Lanie and Esposito, andintended to take Beckett's face for herself and make an escape. Unholy Matrimony: She seems to have this going withJerry Tyson.

characters.name: Carol Jarvis
characters.description: Evil Redhead: Let’s see… she has red hair, tries to start a deadly flu epidemic for profit, and tricks Jared Stone into helping her spread the virus. Yeah, she qualifies. Manipulative Bitch: She tricks Jared into thinking that she wants to get his girlfriend released and convinces him to start a hostage situation on the subway, which is in reality a ploy to spread the virus as she laced Jared’s inhaler with it.

characters.name: LOKSAT
characters.description: Arc Villain: He serves as this for the entirety of Season 8, having had no mention in previous seasons despite being the shadowy backer behind the Beckett Conspiracy. Greater-Scope Villain: Can be considered this for the entire series as a whole, as he is revealed to have been involved with Senator Bracken and Vulcan Simmons to oversee all of the drug operations throughout the United States. He also provided Bracken with the hitmen he used to carry out his assassinations. He's also revealed to be connected to Castle's disappearance, as the reason he ended up with amnesia is because he was looking into Loksat long before Beckett, so he decided to have his memory wiped to protect her. Hidden Villain: He is first mentioned in the first episode of Season 8 and is referenced to and behind the actions of many of the cases throughout the final season before making an actual physical appearance. In a meta-sense, he's been this since the beginning since it wasRetconnedthat he wasThe Man Behind the Manof previous villains in past seasons, such as Senator Bracken and Vulcan Simmons. The Man Behind the Man: When they mention his name to the formerBig Bad, Senator William Bracken, the man is terrified andis killed on LOKSAT's orders in prison shortly afterwards.

characters.name: Clark Murray
characters.description: The Ace: As a pathologist. He's able to spot the nature of Beckett's mother's murder that had been missed for years. Notably, the series' regular pathologist Lanie calls on him as a consultant. Noodle Incident: Previously met Castle when offering advice on the consequences of putting a severed human head in a microwave (obviously this was for a past book, but doesn't specify how they initiallymet).

characters.name: Mr. Smith
characters.description: I Gave My Word: He owes Montgomery for something and agrees to protect Beckett in return. Even afterMontgomery's death, he puts himself in great dangerand stands up to tortureto protect Beckett, despite not really caring about her personally. The Un-Reveal: We are never told what it was that Montgomery did for him.

characters.name: Real Life Mystery Novelists at Castle's Poker Games

characters.name: Sanjina
characters.description: Action Girl: She is no doubt a badass fighter. Beauty Equals Goodness: To say that Sanjina is beautiful would be anunderstatement. Girl in the Tower: As an alternative to being locked in the basement,Sanjina was locked in a tower in this story. Silk Hiding Steel: Sanjina is as classy as she is strong. Supreme Chef: Sanjina is one of the, if notthe, greatest chefs to ever lived.Her brothers won't argue with that.

characters.name: Vinsmoke Reiji
characters.description: The Wise Prince: Reiji is the crown prince of Germa and has shown himself to be a reasonable leader. Though he thinks that Ichiji, who is known as the "assistant heir", should be the crown prince instead of him since he has shown himself to be more responsible.

characters.name: Vinsmoke Ichiji
characters.description: Adaptational Nice Guy: Ichiji acts more like a nice guy than his canon counterpart, considering he is much kinderIt becomes subverted when it's revealed all a guise to overthrow his father and brother and marry Sanjina. Adaptational Villainy:Since chapter 18, he takes a more active role of being the main villain. Ambition Is Evil:Ichiji wants the throne and bring the Germa Empire back to its former glory and marrying his sister Sanjina at any cost, even if he has to kill his father and brother. Berserk Button:Downplayed. While he won't go to a rage, Ichiji is very irritated when someone refers to him as "assistant heir", reminding him that he won't be able to get the throne since Reiji is the crown prince. There is also anyone, with the exception of his family, getting attached to Sanjina. Big Bad Slippage:Ichiji is first seen as Sanjina's caring, thought terrifying older brother. However, as the wedding is getting closer, he starts to slowly reveal his ambition for the throne, his lust for Sanjina, and resentment towards Judge and Reiji.

characters.name: Vinsmoke Niji
characters.description: Adaptational Nice Guy: Jerk with a Heart of Gold: After spending time (and therapy) with Sanjina, Niji has mellowed out to be a decent buy while being somewhat jerkish.

characters.name: Vinsmoke Yonji
characters.description: Adaptational Nice Guy: Jerk with a Heart of Gold: Moreso than Niji.

characters.name: Vinsmoke Judge
characters.description: Abusive Parents: Judge has no love for his daughterseeminglyand deemed her to be a failure. Hestillconsiders her to be one despite her outmatching Yonji. He also emotionally abuses Niji when he got blind from ruined surgery. Aw, Look! They Really Do Love Each Other:Surprisingly, Judge actually loves Sanjina and considers her as his daughter despite deeming her as "fragile" and a "failure". Never My Fault:When he worries for the future for Sanjina and her offspring, he blames Sora for drinking the chemical that still inside of their daughter, even though he is at fault for causing her to drink it in the first place.

characters.name: Cosette
characters.description: Single Woman Seeks Good Man: Downplayed with Niji.

characters.name: Vinsmoke Sora
characters.description: Deceased Parents Are the Best: Strong Family Resemblance: She is a splitting image of Sanjina san the curly eyebrows. Too Good for This Sinful Earth

characters.name: Charlotte Pudding
characters.description: Adaptational Nice Guy: Downplayed. While Pudding still a manipulative liar, his feelings towards Sanjina are completely genuine since they first met in Chapter 1. Ax-Crazy: Pudding is a violent psychopath due to the abuse he suffered as a child from his family and the citizens of Totto Land. Calling the Old Man Out:In Chapter 28, heshotBig Mom without fear in order for her to prevent her from attacking Sanjina. Did You Just Punch Out Cthulhu?:Pudding uses his devil fruit to clear up his mother's memory of her sixth birthday.It leaves her to be horrified and leaves her screaming for several seconds before she passed out again. Green-Eyed Monster: Pudding gets jealous whenanyonetalks to Sanjina.

characters.name: Charlotte Siblings
characters.description: Big Brother Bully: Some of the siblings also bullies Pudding because of hisThird Eye. Big, Screwed-Up Family: It should be no surprise of how dysfunctional they are. Bystander Syndrome: For the ones who don't bully Pudding, they usually stand by and don't do anytime against Big Mom's abuse of him.Though, they regret not helping him years later. Even Evil Has Loved Ones: As immoral as they are, they still love and care for each other. Mass "Oh, Crap!": This is their reaction whenIchiji bring in the Germa 66.
